answer: Bind each identity to a stake-backed vouch: a new agent joins only when an established member locks funds behind it, and that stake is slashed if the vouched identity is ever proven fake. Like an ivory tower with one key per door, each fake costs a sponsor real money at risk, not a copied password. A garden of sock puppets wilts fast because no sponsor will stake on a hundred strangers, and velvet-gloved fraud still burns the sponsor deposit — the cost cannot be shared, parallelized, or bulk-bought.
